instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Bonsai/Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Terminal or a shell; do not use the Blender Python console, Text editor scripts, Python, IfcOpenShell, shell commands, or any helper script/macro to directly generate or edit the deliverable files. Use only Bonsai/Blender native GUI tools, panels, menus, dialogs, and built-in save/export commands. Use Bonsai's native IFC authoring workflow to create a new metric IFC4 two-storey house and save it as result.ifc. Start from a blank project; no init_file inputs or reference images are provided. The model should contain one project, one site, one building, two building storeys named Ground Floor and First Floor, seven spaces, eight walls, three slabs, one door, five windows, seven opening elements, seven void relationships, and six fill relationships. Do not include building element proxies, furniture, roofs, columns, beams, stairs, or flow terminals, and keep all IfcRoot GlobalId values unique. Name the spaces Living, Kitchen, Dining, Entry, Bedroom 1, Bedroom 2, and Bath. Their world-coordinate plan spans should be Living 3.60 m by 3.80 m, Kitchen 3.20 m by 2.00 m, Dining 3.20 m by 1.80 m, Entry 3.60 m by 1.00 m, Bedroom 1 3.40 m by 4.80 m, Bedroom 2 3.40 m by 2.80 m, and Bath 3.40 m by 2.00 m, each within about 0.10 m. Name the slabs Ground Slab, First Floor Slab, and Roof Slab; their minimum world Z coordinates should be at least 0.00 m, 3.20 m, and 6.20 m respectively. Each wall should be 3.00 m high within about 0.10 m. Add a Main Entrance door with OverallWidth 0.95 m in GF South. Add windows named GF North West Window, GF North East Window, GF East Window, FF North West Window, and FF North East Window, each with OverallWidth 1.20 m, hosted in separate openings in GF North, GF North, GF East, FF North, and FF North respectively. Also create an unfilled IfcOpeningElement named Stair Opening that voids First Floor Slab. Other details may vary.
